top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a distinct conceptual step, magic-wavelength lattice trapping, whose 10^-18 performance has been reproduced by independent laboratories with different atoms and whose systematics are understood from atomic structure theory. The two-name allocation (Katori for the proposal and first demonstration, Ye for record accuracy and many-body clock physics) is clean and defensible with a citation resting on invention and realisation, not on unverified fundamental-physics limits. P002 is a strong, genuine discovery but has an attribution gap (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, deceased Zhang, 3D work), a one-group first observation and a 2016 overlap question, so I rank it second; an award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Lindroth is a close collaborator of 2023 laureate L'Huillier and works in attosecond and atomic precision theory, but has no documented direct tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp.
